$comment: Commands that appear in a PR-triggered workflow and are NOT auto-classified
by a rule in preflight.mjs (#3150). Every one carries the reason it is not a
gate a builder can usefully run before pushing.
The rules in preflight.mjs classify the mechanical majority -- `npm run lint:*`,
`npm run check:*`, `npm run typecheck -w`, `npm run test -w`, `npm run build -w`,
`node --test` are gates; `npm ci`, `npx playwright install` and anything carrying
shell syntax are not. This file is only the residue, and its job is to be SMALL
and ARGUED.
A row may be marked `(redundant)` when the rules alone would already answer
not-a-gate without it. NONE is, at this head: removing the metacharacter rule
-- the change that closed the escape class -- made every row load-bearing.
No count is stated here on purpose. preflight.test.mjs re-derives the split by
classifying each row against an EMPTY map, and that test is what caught this
very change; a hand-written total had already gone stale twice in two rounds.
preflight.test.mjs fails when a command matches no rule and has no entry here, so
a new CI step cannot join the workflow without someone deciding which it is. That
is the whole mechanism: #3135 added `check:route-modules` to Backend checks and no
builder battery learned about it for a week, which is the fourth incident #3150
was filed for.
It fails in the other direction too: an entry here that no workflow runs any more
is stale and fails the same test, so this file cannot accumulate dead rows the way
a hand-maintained gate list does.
TWO SHAPES NEITHER HALF SEES, both written down rather than guarded:
1. A `working-directory:` on a gate step. It is discarded, so the battery
would run that gate from the repository root. All four live uses sit on
an excluded command, so this is latent.
2. A gate in a local composite action whose IDENTITY is a `with:` input.
Every rule and every shield entry begins with a LITERAL head, and
`node "${{ inputs.script }}"` is not one, so the command matches
nothing. That is exactly how the one action in the tree is built:
advisory-gate-comment takes the script path as a `with:` input and is
the ADVISORY half of BOTH coupling pairs (docs-coupling.yml and
design-system-coupling.yml). Note the boundary: a templated ARGUMENT on
a literal head IS caught -- only head-templating hides. Catching this
would redden that legitimate action, so it is documented instead, and
preflight.test.mjs PINS BOTH HALVES so this paragraph cannot drift from
the behaviour.
A third shape used to be here and is now guarded: a gate written LITERALLY
into an action file, at any depth. compositeActionGates() refuses one
outright -- shallowly, without resolving `uses:` across the tree, because a
gate does not belong there in the first place: a builder's battery cannot
discover it. It has no escape hatch in this map on purpose; the remedy its
failure names is to move the command into a workflow, where a row here can
argue it like everything else.

notGates.node scripts/ci/change-classifier.mjs: CI plumbing, not a check: it writes the `changes` job's surface outputs to $GITHUB_OUTPUT so the other jobs know whether to run. This battery calls classifyChangedFiles() directly for the same answer.
notGates.node scripts/ci/qa-freshness.mjs: Promotion gate for dev -> main, and it reads the QA run history of the DEPLOYED environment. Nothing a builder can run or influence before pushing a feature branch.
notGates.node scripts/ci/operator-verify-close-gu: Reads the pull request that does not exist yet at pre-push time. Its own suite (operator-verify-close-guard.test.mjs) is collected by `node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs`, which IS in the battery.
notGates.node scripts/ci/db-concurrency-proof.mjs: Nightly advisory-lock deadlock proof (#2208). Needs the CI Postgres service and a report file the workflow produces; It IS pull_request-triggered, path-filtered to the advisory-lock files, so a builder touching those does get this job -- but its Postgres service and report file are CI's, not theirs.
notGates.npm run db:schema-smoke -w packages/back: Applies every migration to a real Postgres and PREPAREs the money-path queries. It is a genuine gate, but it needs a live database -- a builder without one would see it red for the wrong reason, which is the silent-skip failure this battery exists to avoid. Run it deliberately when touching migrations.
notGates.npm run test:visual -w packages/frontend: Playwright visual regression against baseline PNGs. Needs browsers and a built app; the Design visual regression job owns it and it is advisory on dev (epic #2632 step O2).
notGates.npm run test:visual:dark -w packages/fro: The dark-mode half of the same visual regression job, same reason.
notGates.npm run test:e2e:gate -w packages/fronte: Frontend browser smoke -- Playwright against a built app. Needs `npx playwright install`, which the battery deliberately does not run on a builder's machine.
notGates.npm run smoke:pack -w packages/connect: Packs the connect tarball and installs it in a scratch directory. Minutes of npm work with network access; the Install-path smoke job owns it.
notGates.npx playwright install --with-deps chrom: Browser provisioning, not a check. It downloads a Chromium build and its system dependencies, which is minutes of network on a machine that may already have one.
notGates.npm ci: Dependency install, not a check. A builder already has node_modules; re-running it here would be the slowest step in the battery and would prove nothing about the diff.
notGates.npm run test -w packages/backend -- s: The nightly DB concurrency proof's vitest invocation. Same reason as db-concurrency-proof.mjs above: CI's Postgres service plus a report file. Also pull_request-triggered on those paths, so 'nightly' names its schedule, not its only trigger.
notGates.BODY=$(printf '%s\\n' \"\\`db-concurr: PROSE, not a command: the `gh issue` body db-concurrency-proof.yml files when its proof fails, which QUOTES a repro command (`npm run test -w packages/backend -- ...`) inside markdown. The only corpus command the gate-shaped-anywhere rule flips, and the reason that rule is affordable: closing the escape class by position-free rule instead of by separator list costs exactly this one row.
notGates.node -e \"\n const pg = require('pg');\: An inline `node -e` PROGRAM, not a command a builder runs: db-concurrency-proof.yml's Postgres version probe, which opens a pg.Client against the CI service. The only corpus command the metacharacter rule used to silence on its own, and the entire price of removing that rule -- which is what closed the escape class the first four review rounds each found one instance of.
